title: Glossary of Terms for Quality Assurance and Good Laboratory Practices (ST/NAR/26/Rev.1) - Arabic edition
title_ar: مسرد مصطلحات ضمان الجودة والممارسات المختبرية السليمة
publisher: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (United Nations, New York)
key_findings: Official UN Arabic edition (V.11-88111, November 2012; the English Rev.1 is dated December 2009) of a glossary built for national drug-testing and forensic laboratories; each entry gives the Arabic term with its English headword and a definition.

Gives authoritative Arabic equivalents used in this library: chain of custody = سلسلة الحراسة / سلسلة الأدلة; contamination = تلوّث; confirmatory test = اختبار تأكيدي; screening/presumptive test = اختبار فرز (اختبار أولي أو اختبار افتراضي); false positive/negative = إيجابي زائف / سلبي زائف; blind sample = عيّنة محجوبة; double blind = أسلوب الحجب المزدوج.

Also: accreditation = اعتماد; proficiency testing = اختبار الجدارة; uncertainty = اللايقين (الريبة); validation = التثبّت; verification = التحقّق; traceability = تتبّعية; expert witness = شاهد خبير; peer review = استعراض الأقران (النظراء); technical review = استعراض تقني; reference material = مادة مرجعية; known standard/exemplar = معيار معروف / عيّنة نموذجية; crime/forensic laboratory = مختبر جنائي.
Recommends that 'not detected' should not be used as a synonym for 'negative' - a terminology point that supports ATHAR's 'detection is not causation / not detected is not absent' lesson.
athar_applications: Primary authoritative source for ATHAR's Arabic glossary in quality assurance, sampling, error and testing terms (arabic_forensic_glossary.csv).
Use its pair 'اختبار فرز/افتراضي' vs 'اختبار تأكيدي' verbatim in lab #15 ('المادة س').
Use 'عيّنة محجوبة' and 'الحجب' as the official Arabic basis for ATHAR's 'blind verification' wording.
limitations: Drug-testing focus: no entries for pattern evidence (fingerprints, handwriting), likelihood ratio, propositions or cognitive bias.
Arabic text in the PDF uses a legacy font encoding; terms were read via text extraction and must be proof-read against the printed PDF before publication.
Some choices differ from other UN bodies (e.g., UNTERM records 'سلسلة العهدة' for chain of custody).

title: Unified Medical Dictionary (UMD), 5th edition - online English-Arabic medical terminology database
title_ar: المعجم الطبي الموحد
authors: WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean
publisher: World Health Organization, Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean (EMRO)
key_findings: WHO-EMRO dictionary with over 200,000 English-Arabic entries; begun in Baghdad in the 1960s under the Arab Medical Union and maintained by EMRO since 1973 with Arab academies and ministries; each Arabic entry carries a usage flag (e.g., 'موحد' = unified) and sometimes a regional-usage note (e.g., local usage - Egypt).

Queried entries used in ATHAR: forensic medicine = الطب الشرعي; forensic physician = طبيب شرعي; medicolegal = طبي شرعي; forensic pathology = الباثولوجيا الشرعية; forensic odontology/dentistry = طب الأسنان الشرعي; forensic anthropology = الأنثربولوجيا الطبية الشرعية; autopsy: no standalone entry returned on re-query; the three renderings الصفة التشريحية / فتح الجثة / تشريح الجثة come from 'autopsy data' entries (معطيات ...). [Corrected/Clarified 2026-10-27 by deep-card review]

Statistics entries: likelihood ratio = نسبة الترجيح; odds ratio = نسبة الأرجحية; odds = أرجحية; prior/posterior probability = احتمال مسبق / احتمال لاحق; false positive = إيجابي كاذب; positive predictive value = القيمة التنبؤية الإيجابية; prevalence = انتشار; inconclusive = نتيجة غير قاطعة; uncertainty = ارتياب; confirmation bias = التحيز التأكيدي; informed consent = موافقة مستنيرة.

Fingerprint entries: fingerprint = بصمة; fingerprint pattern = طراز البصمة; loop pattern = طراز العروة; arch pattern = طراز القوس; whorl pattern = طراز الدوامة; dermal/papillary ridges = الأعراف الجلدية / الحروف الحلمية; dactyloscopy = فحص البصمات.
athar_applications: Key evidence that 'likelihood ratio' is 'نسبة الترجيح' in unified Arabic medical usage while 'نسبة الأرجحية' is the unified term for 'odds ratio' - ATHAR's wave-1 Arabic label 'نسبة الأرجحية' for LR must be changed to avoid a statistical false friend.
Source for fingerprint pattern names and death-investigation terms in the glossary.
limitations: Medical/epidemiological dictionary: entries are defined for clinical contexts, not forensic evaluation; 'manner of death' is rendered 'ظروف الوفاة', which may not match forensic usage.
Several entries are flagged as local (Egyptian) usage; regional variants must be recorded.
Online access; reuse terms beyond '(c) WHO' not stated - cite terms individually, do not copy the database.

title: UNTERM - United Nations Terminology Database (English-Arabic forensic and justice entries)
authors: United Nations Department for General Assembly and Conference Management and participating UN-system bodies
publisher: United Nations
key_findings: Public multilingual database of UN-system terminology; each record shows the contributing body (UNOV/UNODC, UNHQ, UNOG, ICAO, WHO...) and a validation status.

Validated forensic entries used in ATHAR: forensics/forensic science = علم الأدلة الجنائية (UNOV); forensic science laboratory = المختبر الجنائي (UNOV); reference sample = عيّنة مرجعية (UNOV); digital forensics = الاستدلال الجنائي الرقمي (UNOV); digital evidence = دليل رقمي (UNHQ); preservation of evidence = صون الأدلة / الحفاظ على الأدلة (UNHQ); Crime Scene Examiner = باحث في مسرح الجريمة (UNHQ).
Chain of custody appears as سلسلة العهدة (preferred) and تسلسل العهدة (legal context, OPCW-related record); chain-of-custody records = سجلات تسلسل العهدة (validated).

Justice and ethics entries: presumption of innocence = قرينة البراءة; burden of proof = عبء الإثبات; expert report = تقرير الخبير / التقرير الفني; expert witness = شاهد خبير; informed consent = موافقة مستنيرة; best interests of the child = مصالح الطفل الفضلى; confirmation bias = تحيز تأكيدي (UNHQ); false positive = نتيجة إيجابية كاذبة (WHO); impartiality = حياد / عدم تحيز; AFIS = نظام التعرف الآلي على بصمات الأصابع.
athar_applications: Second authoritative pillar of the glossary; resolves the chain-of-custody split (UNODC glossary 'سلسلة الحراسة' vs UNTERM 'سلسلة العهدة') in favour of 'سلسلة العهدة' as the ATHAR preferred form, with the others as alternatives.
Provides UN-standard Arabic for the justice vocabulary used in case endings (قرينة البراءة، عبء الإثبات).
limitations: Many forensic terms (likelihood ratio, latent print, minutiae, inconclusive, class characteristics) have no UNTERM record.
Records come from different bodies and sometimes conflict; validation status varies (validated / internally approved / none).
Accessed through the public search interface/API; no reuse licence stated.

title: INTERPOL - Forensics pages in Arabic (Fingerprints, DNA, Disaster Victim Identification, Facial recognition)
title_ar: الإنتربول - الأدلة الجنائية
publisher: INTERPOL
key_findings: Official Arabic pages use: الأدلة الجنائية (forensics), البصمة الوراثية (DNA / DNA profile), سمات البصمة الوراثية (DNA profiles), بصمات الأصابع, منظومة التبين الآلي لبصمات الأصابع (AFIS), تحديد هوية ضحايا الكوارث (DVI), تحديد سمات الوجه (facial recognition), القياسات الحيوية (biometrics), مسرح الجريمة.
States that DNA and fingerprints can both link and exclude ('تبرئة' / 'إبعاد التهمة عن شخص بريء'), and that profiles are exchanged as alphanumeric codes without nominal data.
Fingerprint page describes an optional 'confirmed' search route in which two INTERPOL fingerprint experts review candidate decisions, versus a 'lights-out' automated route.
Also describes fingerprints as unique and unchanging - an institutional claim that ATHAR must present with the scientific caveats of the wave-1 library (error rates, PCAST).
athar_applications: Source for Gulf/Levant institutional Arabic (البصمة الوراثية as the common Arabic label for forensic DNA) and for the two-expert review idea used in lab #1.
Example for the 'institutional claim vs scientific limit' teaching pattern (KO-FC-04B-005).
limitations: Outreach web pages, not technical standards; uniqueness claims are stated without error-rate discussion.
Database sizes change; figures not reused.
A 2015 Arabic fact sheet (COM/FS/2015-02/FS-01 'تحديد البصمة الوراثية') exists but is superseded by the web page.

title: Arabic translation of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 - General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories (QCC Abu Dhabi publication S01)
title_ar: المتطلبات العامة لكفاءة مختبرات الفحص والمعايرة (ترجمة عربية)
authors: Abu Dhabi Quality and Conformity Council
publisher: Abu Dhabi Quality and Conformity Council (QCC) - Jawdah portal
key_findings: Arabic translation (1st ed. 2018) approved by the Emirates Authority for Standardization and Metrology on 23 Sept 2018; states that the English text prevails in case of conflict.

Terminology: impartiality = الحيادية; competence = الكفاءة; measurement uncertainty = ارتياب القياس; metrological traceability = السلسلة المترولوجية; decision rule = قاعدة القرار; proficiency testing = اختبار جدارة; validation = التثبّت; verification = التحقق; nonconforming work = الأعمال غير المطابقة; interlaboratory comparison = مقارنة مخبرية خارجية; sampling = أخذ العينات.
athar_applications: Gulf-standard Arabic for quality vocabulary; confirms 'التثبّت' (validation) and 'اختبار الجدارة' (proficiency testing) independently of UNODC.
Supports ATHAR's Arabic wording for accreditation lessons (KO-FC-04-030).
limitations: Not an ISO publication; translation status is national; the PDF could not be re-downloaded by script (connection reset) and was read through WebFetch only.
Standard text is copyrighted: cite terms, never reproduce clauses (checklist item ح1).

title: The College of Forensic Sciences at Naif Arab University for Security Sciences: Leadership in Forensic Sciences in the Arab World
title_ar: كلية علوم الأدلة الجنائية في جامعة نايف العربية للعلوم الأمنية: الريادة في علوم الأدلة الجنائية في العالم العربي
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Institutional history by the college's dean and vice-dean: NAUSS forensic laboratory grew from 1980s drug-identification courses run with the UN drug-control programme, became a UN-designated regional training centre, and became a college in 2004; master's programmes began 2009 (first graduates 2012).

Four departments: forensic chemistry (الكيمياء الجنائية), forensic biology (الأحياء الجنائية), 'forensic natural sciences' i.e. physical evidence and documents (الطبيعيات الجنائية), and crime scene (مسرح الجريمة); reports 331 applied training programmes with 4,486 Arab participants from 1988 to 2013.

Arabic course terminology printed in the article includes الأدلة الزهيدة (trace evidence), التنميط الجيني (genetic profiling), الحاسوب الجنائي والجرائم الإلكترونية, فحص الوثائق, تحقيق الشخصية (personal identification).
athar_applications: Primary Arab institutional source for the 'Arab forensic education' section and for the NAUSS-specific term 'الأدلة الزهيدة' (trace evidence) recorded as a regional variant.
Identifies NAUSS as the natural partner for a terminology workshop and expert review (gap G05).
limitations: Self-description by the institution's leadership (promotional tone); figures not independently verified.
Describes the 2014 structure; NAUSS later reorganised (forensic sciences now within the College of Criminal Justice per the current programme page [ATH-SRC-0784]).

title: Arab Society for Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine (ASFSFM) - official page and Arab Scientific Working Groups
title_ar: الجمعية العربية لعلوم الأدلة الجنائية والطب الشرعي
authors: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences
key_findings: Society established 4/6/2013 by NAUSS's Supreme Council; the page lists about 360 members/experts, active/associate/honorary membership, and a mandate to unify methods and develop policies for accreditation and recognition of Arab forensic institutions.

Six Arab Scientific Working Groups: crime scene, forensic toxicology, digital forensic evidence, forensic entomology, forgery and counterfeiting, forensic DNA evidence; groups issue guidelines and SOPs as Arab references.
Publishes AJFSFM (open access, Arabic and English; the page says it is indexed in Scopus and DOAJ).
athar_applications: Partner map: the working groups are the most relevant Arab bodies for reviewing ATHAR's crime-scene, document, DNA and digital labs.
Evidence that Arab forensic standard-setting exists but is younger and narrower than OSAC/ENFSI; ATHAR should cite Arab guidelines where they exist and international ones otherwise.
limitations: Institutional page; membership and indexing claims not independently checked; no list of published guidelines on the page.
No terminology/glossary output is mentioned.

title: Third Arab International Conference on Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine, ASFSFM2017: Conference Report
title_ar: المؤتمر العربي الدولي الثالث لعلوم الأدلة الجنائية والطب الشرعي ASFSFM2017: تقرير المؤتمر
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Conference held 21-23 Nov 2017 at NAUSS, Riyadh; about 720 specialists from 33 countries.

Seven recommendations include: create accreditation, quality and recognition standards for Arab forensic institutions under a specialised body; activate Arab scientific working groups to unify standards; standardise forensic terminology (توحيد المصطلحات); develop continuing education and criteria for recognising expert practitioners.
athar_applications: Documented Arab professional acknowledgement that forensic terminology is NOT yet unified - supports marking many glossary entries 'proposed' and running an expert terminology workshop.
Shows that region-wide accreditation of Arab forensic institutions was an open goal in 2017.
limitations: Meeting report; recommendations do not prove implementation.
Attendance figures are the organisers' own.

title: 2nd Arab Forensic Science & Forensic Medicine Meeting, ASFSFM 2016: Meeting Report
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (journal licence per DOAJ; article PDF footer)
key_findings: Meeting held 8-9 Nov 2016 at NAUSS; about 166 specialists from 16 countries.

Goals: unify quality standards across Arab forensic laboratories and forensic-medicine practice; recommendations include an Arab institutional accreditation programme, Arab working groups (including disaster victim identification) and published guidelines.
athar_applications: Corroborates ATH-SRC-1707: region-level accreditation and harmonisation were aspirations, not achievements, in 2016-2017.
limitations: Meeting report; the journal's own citation line shows an inconsistent volume/year.

AUDIT-W2 2026-10-27: rights corrected UNKNOWN -> OPEN_LICENSE CC BY-NC 4.0 (DOAJ journal record ISSN 1658-6794; WebFetch of the article PDF shows 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial License'). NAUSS OJS returned HTTP 404 to automated requests on 2026-10-27 (url, verification_url and DOI landing); DOI metadata confirmed via Crossref/OpenAlex/DOAJ. Key findings (8-9 Nov 2016, 166+ specialists, 16 countries; accreditation programme, Arab working groups incl. DVI, guidelines) confirmed in the PDF.

title: Arab Scientific Working Group for Forensic Toxicology (ASWGFT): Guidelines for Method Validation in Forensic Toxicology (2017) and Version 2.0 in Arabic (2020)
title_ar: المبادئ التوجيهية في مختبرات السموم الجنائية: التحقق من صلاحية الطرق التحليلية (الإصدار الثاني)
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: First version published in English (AJFSFM 1(6), 2017, doi 10.26735/16586794.2017.013); Version 2.0 issued 2020 with the Arabic title 'المبادئ التوجيهية في مختبرات السموم الجنائية: التحقق من صلاحية الطرق التحليلية' (AJFSFM 2(1)).

Abstract states that validated, reliable analytical data are essential before toxicological findings are used as evidence; unreliable results can be challenged in court and can lead to unfair judgments.
Arabic rendering of method validation here is 'التحقق من صلاحية الطرق التحليلية' - differs from UNODC/QCC 'التثبّت'.
athar_applications: Evidence that an Arab regional toxicology-validation guideline exists (relevant to wave-1 open question on SWGTOX vs ANSI/ASB 036): cite it as the Arab reference at principle level only.
Source for the glossary's alternative 'التحقق من صلاحية الطريقة' for method validation.
limitations: Content not reproduced or read in full; ATHAR uses only the principle that methods must be validated.
Safety: toxicology details stay out of ATHAR (protocol §1.4).

title: Standard Practices and Guidelines in Forensic Entomology (Arab Scientific Working Group for Forensic Entomology)
title_ar: الممارسات القياسية والمبادئ التوجيهية في علم الحشرات الجنائي
authors: Arab Scientific Working Group for Forensic Entomology
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Arabic best-practice protocol (AJFSFM 4(2): 131-157) by the Arab working group covering definitions of key terms, collection of entomological evidence, minimum post-mortem interval estimation methods, quality assurance and case reporting (an English version appeared in 2019, doi 10.26735/16586794.2019.023).
Abstract frames the guideline as needed so that entomological evidence is defensible in court.
athar_applications: Shows the Arab working groups publish Arabic definitions of key terms - a model for ATHAR's glossary format; ATHAR uses only the term 'علم الحشرات الجنائي' and the idea that PMI estimates are minimum intervals.
limitations: Topic is NOT suitable for teen content beyond the name of the discipline (decomposition imagery); used only for terminology and as evidence of Arab standard-setting.

title: Developing Academic Educational Programs in Forensic Sciences: A Continuous Need to Achieve Professionalism in Forensic Work and Serve Justice
title_ar: تطوير البرامج التعليمية الأكاديمية في علوم الأدلة الجنائية: حاجة مستمرة لتحقيق الاحترافية في العمل الجنائي وخدمة العدالة
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Review (AJFSFM 4(1): 65-81) arguing that criminal-justice systems need forensic graduates with demonstrated professionalism and that education must be developed across programmes, curricula, pedagogy, assessment, practice facilities, research and partnerships between universities and forensic laboratories/police.
Provides a worldwide review of forensic education approaches as a basis for Arab programme development (abstract).
athar_applications: Supports positioning ATHAR as 'pre-professional scientific literacy' rather than forensic training, and suggests university forensic departments as content reviewers.
Arabic-language framing of forensic education useful for partner pitches.
limitations: Review/position paper; no outcome data on Arab programmes; full text not read beyond the abstract.

title: Review of Current Status of Forensic Medicine and Related Courses at Saudi Universities Offering Medical Programs
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Reviewed forensic-medicine curricula of 65 Saudi universities via their websites and found inconsistencies in credit hours, the year of study in which forensic medicine is taught, and course content (AJFSFM 6(2): 167-180).
Concludes that undergraduate forensic-medicine teaching is not standardised and proposes a model curriculum.
athar_applications: Evidence that even within medicine, forensic education in the region is uneven - realistic background for ATHAR stories (a doctor character may have had little forensic training).
Suggests Saudi medical-school forensic departments as reviewers for death-investigation terminology.
limitations: Website-based review, not curriculum documents or outcomes; Saudi Arabia only.

title: Forensic Medicine in Morocco: Reality and Prospects
title_ar: الطب الشرعي الجنائي في المغرب: واقع وآفاق
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Arabic article (AJFSFM 1(7), 2018) on the current state and prospects of criminal forensic medicine in Morocco (bibliographic record verified; full text not read).
athar_applications: Pointer for Maghreb context in the institutions map; not used for any factual claim beyond its existence.
limitations: Only metadata verified; content not summarised.

title: Using Metadata as Supporting Evidence in Digital Forensic Investigation: A Proposed Model
title_ar: تطويع الميتاداتا كدليل مساند ضمن عمليات التحقيق الجنائي الرقمي: نموذج مقترح
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Arabic article (AJFSFM 3(2): 360-377) proposing a model for using metadata (الميتاداتا) as supporting evidence (دليل مساند) in digital criminal investigation (التحقيق الجنائي الرقمي).
athar_applications: Attests Arabic forensic usage of 'الميتاداتا' and 'دليل مساند' alongside UN 'البيانات الوصفية' - recorded as regional variants in the glossary; supports the 'metadata corroborates, it does not prove alone' framing of lab #8.
limitations: Only the abstract was read; ATHAR does not use any technical procedure from it.

title: Handling E-evidence in Egyptian and Comparative Legislation: A Comparative Analytical Study
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Examines the characteristics of electronic evidence, its legal authenticity in Egyptian law, requirements for its collection and admissibility before criminal courts and the procedures for gathering and documenting it (AJFSFM 6(1): 37-68).
Concludes that the changing, intangible nature of digital evidence affects its reliability before criminal courts (abstract).
athar_applications: Supports the ATHAR rule that digital evidence in Arab settings must be collected by authorised officials and documented - the teen hero hands over, never extracts (consistent with ARAB_CRIMINAL_PROCEDURE_CONTEXT.md §5.2).
limitations: Legal analysis from abstract only; Egypt's new Criminal Procedure Law (174/2025) is not covered.

title: The Language of Forensic Experts: A Commentary on the Sally Clark Case (1999-2002)
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Commentary published in the Arab regional journal (AJFSFM 1(9): 1286-1295) on how expert language and statistics were misused in the Sally Clark case (bibliographic record verified; abstract not available via Crossref).
athar_applications: Shows that the prosecutor's-fallacy lesson already circulates in Arab forensic literature - an Arab-published citation for labs #11 and #24.
limitations: Full text not read; ATHAR's statistical claims continue to rest on ATH-SRC-0338.

AUDIT-W2 2026-10-27: rights corrected UNKNOWN -> OPEN_LICENSE CC BY-NC 4.0 (DOAJ journal record; OpenAlex 'cc-by-nc', diamond OA). Abstract IS available via OpenAlex (record said not available): adversarial vs inquisitorial expert role; Clark later shown innocent; experts now see testifying as a risk. NAUSS landing page returned 404 to automated requests on 2026-10-27; WebSearch lists the article page and PDF. internal_storage_permission left not_established pending a direct read of the article footer.

title: Interpretation of Evidence: The Key to Conveying Information to Court
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Article in AJFSFM 1(9): 1277-1285 on evidence interpretation as the key to communicating forensic results to courts (record verified; abstract not available).
athar_applications: Arab-journal citation for the evaluative-reporting lesson (lab #2) next to ENFSI [ATH-SRC-0317]; candidate for checking which Arabic keywords AJFSFM uses for 'likelihood ratio'.
limitations: Full text and Arabic abstract could not be fetched (site returned errors).

title: Dubai Police conducted over 58,000 forensic tests to solve cases in 2023 (General Department of Forensic Science and Criminology press briefing)
publisher: Gulf News
key_findings: Report of a 11 July 2024 briefing: the General Department of Forensic Science and Criminology carried out more than 58,000 forensic tests in 2023; units include DNA (with a Genome Centre launched 2023), fingerprints, crime scene, forensic medicine, toxicology/chemistry, entomology, facial reconstruction and disaster victim identification.

Staff of 280 (172 men, 108 women) with degrees in natural sciences, engineering, medicine, law and police science; the department reports seven ISO certifications without naming each standard in the article.
athar_applications: Story realism: an Arab police forensic department is a large multi-disciplinary scientific service with many women scientists - ATHAR can show female Arab forensic scientists as normal, not exceptional.
Candidate partner/expert-reviewer institution (UAE).
limitations: Journalism based on a police press conference; '99% solved' type claims elsewhere are institutional statistics, not independent evaluations; ISO scope not specified.

title: 'Crime Scene' at Dubai Police lifts 270,000 physical and digital traces since 2023 (Emarat Al Youm / Al Bayan / Gulf News, Oct 2026)
title_ar: «مسرح الجريمة» بشرطة دبي يرفع 270 ألف أثر مادي ورقمي منذ 2023
publisher: Emarat Al Youm (Dubai Media Incorporated)
key_findings: Crime Scene Management Department (إدارة مسرح الجريمة) of the General Department of Forensic Evidence and Criminology (الإدارة العامة للأدلة الجنائية وعلم الجريمة) reports 269,707 physical and digital traces lifted from 2023 to August 2026.

Operational procedures are described as aligned with ISO 17020 (inspection bodies) with annual external audits; tools include barcoded evidence bags (الأحراز), a paperless case-management system, 3D scanning and a digital platform called 'أثر'.
Arabic terms in use: سلسلة عهدة الدليل (chain of custody), الدليل الجنائي, آثار مادية ورقمية, بصمة التربة, علم الحشرات الجنائي.
athar_applications: Gulf institutional Arabic for chain of custody ('سلسلة عهدة الدليل') and evidence packages ('الأحراز') - adopted in the glossary as regional variants.
Realism: crime-scene units work to ISO/IEC 17020, laboratories to ISO/IEC 17025 - the two standards should not be confused in ATHAR stories.
Naming risk: Dubai Police uses the name 'أثر' for a digital platform - flag for the trademark/naming team (11).
limitations: Press coverage of an institutional statement; performance figures are self-reported.
Article says procedures follow ISO 17020; it does not prove accreditation.

title: Abu Dhabi Police Criminal Evidence Department renews its international accreditation (ISO/IEC 17025, UKAS)
publisher: Abu Dhabi Police GHQ
key_findings: Official news item (article text dated 24 July 2012; the URL carries a 2021 republication date) stating that the Criminal Evidence Department renewed ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation from the UK accreditation body UKAS for the fourth consecutive year.
Scope listed includes drug and toxicology testing, alcohol and doping tests, chemical analysis, DNA profiling and forensic biology.
athar_applications: Documented fact that some Gulf police forensic laboratories held ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation from a foreign (UK) body by the early 2010s - useful for the accreditation map and story realism.
limitations: Date ambiguity on the page; current status (2026) not verified.

title: Five Units of Ras Al Khaimah Police's Forensic Laboratory Earn International Accreditation (ISO/IEC 17020 with ILAC G19, EIAC)
authors: Ras Al Khaimah Government Media Office
publisher: Ras Al Khaimah Government Media Office
key_findings: 22 June 2022: Emirates International Accreditation Centre (EIAC) accredited units of the RAK Police forensic laboratory as a type-A inspection body under ISO/IEC 17020:2012 with ILAC G19 (forensic requirements).
Accredited units include autopsy, histopathology and clinical forensic medicine; a women and children unit; fire-traces examination; counterfeit-currency investigation.
athar_applications: Shows national (UAE) accreditation via EIAC and the use of ILAC G19 for forensic units - a concrete example for the accreditation lesson and expert-review questions.
limitations: Government press release; claims of being 'first in the Gulf' are self-reported.

title: Departments of Egypt's Forensic Medicine Authority and their competences after international accreditation (Youm7, 9 Jan 2023)
title_ar: اعرف أقسام الطب الشرعى واختصاصاتها بعد حصول بعضها على شهادة الاعتماد الدولى
publisher: Youm7 (اليوم السابع)
key_findings: Egypt's Forensic Medicine Authority (مصلحة الطب الشرعي, Ministry of Justice) has four competence areas: field forensic medicine (autopsy, examination of injured persons, age estimation, court testimony), forensic medical laboratories (biology, DNA), forensic chemical laboratories (toxicology, drugs, fire accelerants) and the Counterfeiting and Forgery Research administration (إدارة أبحاث التزييف والتزوير: documents, signatures, currency).

Reports accreditation by EGAC (Egyptian Accreditation Council): chemistry/toxicology labs as a testing body for certain drug tests, forgery administration as a type-A inspection body for currency, renewal for the Cairo DNA lab (معمل البصمة الوراثية), and continued accreditation for the morgue, violence clinic and histopathology.
athar_applications: Egyptian institutional vocabulary (أبحاث التزييف والتزوير، البصمة الوراثية، الأحراز) for regional-variant columns; realistic Egyptian setting: document examination sits inside the Ministry of Justice, not the police.
Candidate Egyptian reviewer institution for document-examination labs (#6).
limitations: News summary; the standard numbers (17025 vs 17020) are not named in the article; scope details need confirmation from EGAC's register.

title: More than 28 thousand cases received by the Forensic Medical Services Centre in Riyadh region (Saudi Ministry of Health news, July 2023)
title_ar: أكثر من 28 ألف قضية يستقبلها مركز الخدمات الطبية الشرعية بمنطقة الرياض
authors: Saudi Ministry of Health - Riyadh Region Health
publisher: Ministry of Health, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
key_findings: The Forensic Medical Services Centre (مركز الخدمات الطبية الشرعية) in Riyadh received 28,003 cases in the first half of 2023, mostly poison-control cases plus forensic deaths and living-person forensic cases referred by investigation and prosecution authorities.
Its forensic toxicology services hold ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation from the Saudi Accreditation Center (SAAC) and renewed CAP accreditation.
athar_applications: Saudi institutional realism: forensic medicine and forensic toxicology sit in the Ministry of Health, receiving referrals from the Public Prosecution - different from police-run labs in the UAE.
Documented Saudi national accreditation (SAAC, ISO/IEC 17025) for the institutions map.
limitations: Ministry news item; structure of the national system not described.

title: Poison Control and Forensic Chemistry Centers (Saudipedia entry)
title_ar: مراكز مراقبة السموم والكيمياء الطبية الشرعية
publisher: Saudipedia
key_findings: Ten Ministry of Health poison-control and forensic-chemistry centres (first ones from 1402H/1982 in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province); they serve forensic-medicine departments and list CAP and ISO 17025 accreditation.
athar_applications: Background for the Saudi institutional map only.
limitations: Encyclopedic summary with at least one garbled passage; secondary to ATH-SRC-1723.

title: Jordan, American University of Beirut sign MoU to enhance forensic medicine training (Petra, 16 Feb 2026)
publisher: Jordan News Agency (Petra)
key_findings: Jordan's Ministry of Health and AUB Medical Center signed an MoU so that AUB pathology trainees train at Jordan's National Forensic Medicine Center (المركز الوطني للطب الشرعي) under the Ministry's Chief of Forensic Medicine.
A separate 2022 ministry statement (Jordan News) said forensic medicine remains under Ministry of Health jurisdiction and will not be given to private hospitals.
athar_applications: Confirms the Jordanian forensic-medicine authority is a Ministry of Health national centre (name used by Petra: National Forensic Medicine Center, not 'Institute') - corrects the brief's working name.
Jordan-Lebanon training link is relevant to a Levant expert-review network.
limitations: News item; does not describe the centre's structure or accreditation.

title: Crown Prince visits the Criminal Laboratories and Evidence Department of Jordan's Public Security Directorate (Al-Mamlaka TV)
title_ar: ولي العهد يزور إدارة المختبرات والأدلة الجرمية
publisher: Al-Mamlaka TV
key_findings: Names the Jordanian police forensic body 'إدارة المختبرات والأدلة الجرمية' within the Public Security Directorate; describes its work on criminal and digital evidence and calls for cooperation with universities and the private sector.
athar_applications: Source for the Jordanian term 'الأدلة الجرمية' (Levantine legal usage of جرمي vs Gulf/Egyptian جنائي) in the glossary's regional-variant column; partner map.
limitations: Ceremonial news; no data on sections or accreditation; date on page uncertain (2026).

title: Ministry of Interior: transferring Forensic Evidence to the Ministry of Justice would disrupt our security system (Al-Jarida, Kuwait, Oct 2023)
title_ar: «الداخلية»: نقل «الأدلة الجنائية» إلى «العدل» يخل بمنظومتنا الأمنية
publisher: Al-Jarida (Kuwait)
key_findings: Reports a Kuwaiti MP proposal to move the General Department of Forensic Evidence from the Interior Ministry to the Justice Ministry and the Interior Ministry's objection (integration with crime-scene teams, speed, no recorded problems since 1960).
The Ministry argues neutrality depends on individuals, cites a quality-control unit created in 2008, and says prosecutors can inspect the department's work.
athar_applications: Arab instance of the NAS-2009 debate on independence of forensic labs from police [ATH-SRC-0300] - a balanced discussion card for 16-18 / 18+ (two institutional views, no verdict).
limitations: Only one side's arguments are reported in detail.

title: Internal Security Forces (Lebanon) statement asking relatives of missing persons to provide DNA samples at Judicial Police incident offices (17 Apr 2026)
authors: Internal Security Forces - Directorate General (Public Relations)
publisher: Lebanese Internal Security Forces
key_findings: Official ISF notice: reference DNA samples from relatives are taken at the incident offices of the Judicial Police Unit (وحدة الشرطة القضائية) in eight governorate locations; two direct relatives (parents or children) are preferred, otherwise siblings, with an identity document.
athar_applications: Documents that in Lebanon the Judicial Police (ISF) handles reference-sample collection for identification - institutional realism for a Lebanese setting; illustrates 'reference sample' and 'kinship testing' at concept level.
limitations: Context is mass-casualty identification after attacks: ATHAR must NOT build stories on this real context (sensitivity and safety rules). The notice does not name the laboratory performing analyses; Annahar (Apr 2026) reports testing at a hospital laboratory, so the ISF lab structure remains unverified.

title: Lebanese Ministry of Justice - Forensic Medicine and Criminal Evidence Department (مصلحة الطب الشرعي والأدلة الجنائية) and directories of forensic doctors and sworn experts
title_ar: وزارة العدل اللبنانية - مصلحة الطب الشرعي والأدلة الجنائية
publisher: Ministry of Justice, Lebanese Republic
key_findings: The Ministry's official site lists a 'Forensic Medicine and Criminal Evidence Department' (مصلحة الطب الشرعي والأدلة الجنائية) among its departments, plus public directories of forensic doctors (دليل الأطباء الشرعيين) and of experts sworn before the courts (دليل الخبراء المحلفين لدى المحاكم).
The department detail page itself returned no description at verification time.
athar_applications: Lebanese realism: forensic doctors act as court-appointed/sworn experts listed by the Ministry of Justice - a 'forensic doctor' character in a Lebanese story is appointed by the judiciary (consistent with the investigating-judge model).
limitations: Structure, appointment rules and laboratory capacity not described on the site; needs a Lebanese lawyer/forensic doctor to confirm.

title: Lebanese Republic - Laboratories (QUALEB quality unit, Ministry of Economy and Trade): ISO 17025 support programme
authors: Ministry of Economy and Trade, Lebanon - QUALEB
publisher: Ministry of Economy and Trade, Lebanon
key_findings: About 30 testing laboratories in Lebanon; 11 supported labs were certified to ISO 17025 and gained international accreditation under QUALEB phases I-II; a further nine (energy, university, chambers of commerce, electrical) were in preparation. No forensic laboratory is listed.
athar_applications: Negative evidence for the institutions map: we found no public record of ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for a Lebanese forensic laboratory - an open question for experts.
limitations: Page undated; absence on this page does not prove absence of accreditation.

title: National Scientific and Technical Police Laboratory (DGSN, Morocco) obtains ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation in all disciplines (Hespress, 14 Feb 2024)
title_ar: مختبر الشرطة العلمية ينال شهادة «إيزو»
publisher: Hespress
key_findings: Reports that the DGSN National Scientific and Technical Police Laboratory (المختبر الوطني للشرطة العلمية والتقنية, Casablanca) holds ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation from the US body ANAB, extended in 2024 to all forensic branches (biology, documents, fire and explosives, drugs and toxic substances), for the sixth consecutive year.
athar_applications: Maghreb data point and Moroccan term 'الشرطة العلمية' (scientific police) for the regional-variant column.
limitations: Journalism; scope not checked against ANAB's directory.

title: MSc in Forensic Science (MSFS) - College of Science, United Arab Emirates University
publisher: United Arab Emirates University
key_findings: 30-credit MSc (21 taught + 9 thesis), 2 years full-time or 3 part-time; core areas forensic toxicology, DNA analysis, criminalistics and analytical chemistry; collaboration with law-enforcement and research agencies (not named on the page).
athar_applications: Second Gulf civilian university programme (besides NAUSS) for the education map and possible academic reviewers.
limitations: Page does not state start year, partners or accreditation.

title: Master of Science Program in Forensic Sciences - Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (College of Criminal Justice)
authors: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences
key_findings: Two-year programme taught in English with two tracks - forensic genetics and molecular biology; forensic chemistry and toxicology; requires a science bachelor's and IELTS 5.0; aimed at forensic-laboratory personnel and toxicology analysts; linked to the Saudi occupational role 'Forensic Laboratory Specialist'.
athar_applications: Shows that advanced Arab forensic education is often delivered in English - supports ATHAR's bilingual glossary (Arabic first, English in parentheses) so learners can connect to university study.
Complements ATH-SRC-0784 (MSc in Forensic Evidence).
limitations: Programme page only; no outcome data.

title: Arabic-Illiterate Forensic Handwriting Analysis: A Pilot Study ... Ability of Arabic-Illiterate Examiners to Judge the Accuracy of Simulations of Arabic Signatures
publisher: Journal of the American Society of Questioned Document Examiners
key_findings: Pilot study (JASQDE 17(1): 3-9): 100 native Arabic writers (collected in Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Morocco) produced simulations of two Arabic signatures; two Arabic-literate and two Arabic-illiterate certified examiners rated simulation accuracy on six elements.
No statistically significant difference between literate and illiterate examiner groups on any element; largest (non-significant) gap on slant; illiterate examiners took months longer.
Author lists limits: four examiners, simulations not real forgeries, physical features only (not cultural signature styles).
athar_applications: The only examiner-level evidence we found on Arabic script: it does NOT measure error rates of Arabic handwriting identification, so ATHAR must not transfer the Latin-script black-box rates [ATH-SRC-0333] to Arabic as if measured.
Supports keeping lab #6 on fictional Latin-free 'generated' scripts or labelling Arabic examples 'illustrative'.
limitations: Very small examiner sample; ratings of simulation quality, not identification decisions.

title: The Ability of Forensic Handwriting Examiners to Judge the Quality of Signature Simulations in an Unfamiliar Writing System
publisher: Journal of the American Society of Questioned Document Examiners
key_findings: Four examiners (two fluent in Arabic, two without Arabic) rated 100 freehand simulations of two Arabic signatures for line quality, form and proportion; no significant differences between the teams (JASQDE 13(2): 65-69).
athar_applications: Background for the expert-review question 'do Latin-script findings apply to Arabic?' - answer so far: only small pilot evidence on signatures.
limitations: Tiny sample; author calls for more scripts and elements.

title: Regional and National Variation in Arabic Handwriting (PhD thesis)
publisher: University of Central Lancashire
key_findings: 600 handwriting samples (150 each from Jordan, Morocco, Oman, Tunisia); 10 characters and one word yielded 221 class characteristics (shape, stroke number, pen movement, start point).
Countries formed distinct but overlapping groups (ANOSIM R = 0.321, p = 0.0002); blind tests suggested region/nationality could be predicted with a 'useful degree of accuracy'.
Limited to four of 22 Arab countries and 10 of 28 letters.
athar_applications: Key Arab-script finding for ATHAR: Arabic handwriting carries regional CLASS characteristics - a lab can teach 'class vs individual characteristics' with Arabic letters (e.g., a letter form common in the Maghreb vs the Gulf) without claiming writer identification.
Also a caution: regional inference from handwriting can slide into stereotyping; ATHAR uses fictional regions only.
limitations: Thesis, not peer-reviewed article; overlap between groups means individual-level prediction is uncertain.

title: Management of Dead Bodies after Disasters: A Field Manual for First Responders (Arabic edition)
title_ar: إدارة الجثث بعد وقوع الكوارث: دليل ميداني موجّه إلى المستجيب الأول
authors: International Committee of the Red Cross
International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
publisher: International Committee of the Red Cross
key_findings: Arabic edition (second, updated edition; page shows 2018 posting, metadata 2016) of the ICRC/WHO/PAHO/IFRC field manual: إدارة الجثث بعد وقوع الكوارث: دليل ميداني موجّه إلى المستجيب الأول.
Uses Arabic terms 'التعرف على الموتى' (identification of the dead), توثيق, تسجيل المعلومات, تحليل الحمض النووي; emphasises dignified handling and documentation to enable later identification.
athar_applications: Terminology only (identification, documentation) and the ethical principle of dignity; ATHAR does NOT build teen content on mass-fatality scenarios.
limitations: Sensitive subject; 18+ reference only; content not reproduced.

title: Ethical Principles of Psychologists and Code of Conduct (2002, amended 2010 and 2016) - Standards 3.10, 8.07, 8.08
publisher: American Psychological Association
key_findings: Adopted 2002, effective 2003; amended 2010 and 2016 (effective 1 Jan 2017); no later revision listed at verification.

3.10: for persons legally unable to consent, provide an explanation, seek the person's assent, consider preferences and best interests, and obtain permission from a legally authorised person; document consent/assent.

8.07: deception only when justified by significant scientific, educational or applied value and when non-deceptive alternatives are not feasible; never about procedures expected to cause physical pain or severe emotional distress; explain deception as early as feasible (no later than the end of data collection) and allow withdrawal of data.
8.08: provide prompt debriefing about nature, results and conclusions and correct known misconceptions; minimise harm if debriefing is delayed or withheld.
athar_applications: Normative backbone of BIAS_LAB_ETHICS_FOR_MINORS.md: ATHAR's context-manipulation labs are educational (not research) but adopt the stricter research standard: justification, no-distress topic, disclosure before the session ends, right to withdraw data.
limitations: US professional code for psychologists; binding on members, not on an ed-tech company; educational use of deception in a product is not directly addressed.

title: Ethical Principles and Standards for Developmental Scientists (SRCD, 2021)
authors: Society for Research in Child Development
publisher: Society for Research in Child Development
key_findings: Dated 28 March 2021; 'children' explicitly includes adolescents.

2.a: assent procedures tailored to cognitive, emotional and social maturity; a minor's objection should be ethically binding unless the research offers an important direct benefit available only in the study.
4.d: debriefing as soon as feasible, described in advance during consent; correct post-study misconceptions or harms.

4.e: deception defined as intentional false, misleading or withheld information; allowed only when disclosure would distort behaviour and no non-deceptive alternative exists; not when pain or emotional distress is reasonably expected; explained at the end unless disclosure itself would harm.
5.c: be prepared to stop at any stage if continuation is likely to cause psychological or social harm.
athar_applications: Child-specific standard used to set ATHAR's rules: the child's 'no' is binding (opt-out without penalty), debrief is announced up front ('authorized' framing), and the lab stops if distress signals appear.
limitations: Research standard for scientists; ATHAR applies it by analogy to a commercial learning product.

DUPLICATE: the same SRCD 2021 document was catalogued concurrently by the 07 pilot team as ATH-SRC-2104 (same URL); the merge step should alias one ID to the other (content here is specific to sections 2.a, 4.d, 4.e, 5.c).

title: BPS Code of Human Research Ethics (April 2021)
authors: British Psychological Society Research Ethics working group
publisher: The British Psychological Society
key_findings: ISBN 978-1-85433-792-4. Deception or covert data collection only where essential, no alternative exists, the objective has strong scientific merit and there is a harm-alleviation strategy; if participants are likely to feel discomfort, anger or objection when it is revealed, the deception is inappropriate.
Distinguishes withholding some details of the hypothesis from deliberately misinforming participants about the purpose - especially implying a more benign topic than the real one.
Debriefing: verbal explanation may not remove after-effects; e.g., after inducing a negative mood, restore a positive one before the participant leaves.
Children: consent is a social negotiation; school settings exert compliance pressure; make 'no consequences to saying no' explicit and design questions to which a child can be expected to say no.
athar_applications: Two design rules for ATHAR: (1) prefer WITHHOLDING (two groups get different true context) over FALSE STATEMENTS; (2) end each bias lab with an active mood-restoring/competence-restoring step, not just an explanation.
School deployments must give students a real, penalty-free opt-out.
limitations: UK research code; all rights reserved - paraphrase only.

title: Deception Research Involving Children: Ethical Practices and Paradoxes
publisher: Ethics & Behavior (Taylor & Francis)
key_findings: Commentary (Ethics & Behavior 15(3): 271-287) organising deception research with children around four decision points: scientific validity and social value versus alternatives; avoiding and minimising risk; child assent as a questionable safeguard; and debriefing as both remedy and risk.
athar_applications: Frames ATHAR's protocol: (a) can the same learning be achieved without deception? (b) minimise risk; (c) assent alone is not enough protection; (d) debriefing can itself harm (e.g., embarrassment at being 'fooled' before peers) - so debriefs are private and normalising.
limitations: Conceptual analysis, not empirical; US research context.

title: Acceptability by Parents and Children of Deception in Pediatric Research
publisher: Journal of Developmental & Behavioral Pediatrics (Wolters Kluwer)
key_findings: 94 children (mean age 12.8) and their parents interviewed about 2.5 years after a pain study that used deception; only 25.5% of parents and 13.8% of children spontaneously recalled the deception.

Participants reported positive experiences, comfort with debriefing, no negative change in opinion of researchers, and most would take part again; authors conclude deception can be acceptable when thoughtfully planned and disclosed and suggest studying 'authorized deception'.
athar_applications: Best direct evidence that early adolescents and parents can accept a disclosed, well-debriefed deception - supports allowing context-manipulation labs from about 13 under strict conditions.
Also shows children forget the deception - so the learning point must be re-stated in the debrief and the summary card, not assumed.
limitations: Single Canadian pain-study sample; long recall interval; acceptability was self-reported; not a learning-game context; no Arab sample.

AUDIT-W2 2026-10-27: legal_text_access free_official -> paywalled: Europe PMC/OpenAlex show no open-access copy (isOpenAccess N, not in PMC); the PubMed abstract is free. Metadata confirmed (JDBP 36(2):75-85, 2015); abstract supports both key findings.

title: Children's Understanding of Their Research Rights before and after Debriefing: Informed Assent, Confidentiality, and Stopping Participation
publisher: Child Development (Wiley / OUP)
key_findings: 178 children aged about 8, 10 and 12 in a peer-provocation study: most assented freely without felt pressure; older children understood participation, confidentiality and purpose better than 8-year-olds.
After debriefing, understanding of research rights was largely unchanged and most children still had difficulty describing the research goals.
athar_applications: Debriefing does not automatically produce understanding - ATHAR's debrief must check comprehension with a short question, not just display text.
Supports setting the lower age for context-manipulation labs at 13+, above the ages where understanding was weakest.
limitations: Ages 8-12 only; one US study; research rather than learning context.

title: Children's Attitudes about Experimental Participation: The Effect of Deception and Debriefing
publisher: The Journal of Social Psychology (Taylor & Francis)
key_findings: 33 fifth-grade children rated a deception experiment before debriefing, after debriefing, or after debriefing plus thanks; children viewed participation favourably and debriefing made them view experimentation more positively rather than more sceptically.
athar_applications: Weak but convergent evidence that a respectful debrief with appreciation does not breed cynicism; used only as supporting citation.
limitations: Very small, old, single-site study.

title: Perseverance in Self-Perception and Social Perception: Biased Attributional Processes in the Debriefing Paradigm
publisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (APA)
key_findings: After false success/failure feedback and a standard 'outcome' debriefing, self- and observer impressions persisted; a 'process' debriefing that explicitly explained how impressions persevere generally eliminated the erroneous self-perceptions.
athar_applications: Core design rule: ATHAR debriefs must be PROCESS debriefs - explain why the context changed the judgment and that the effect can persist after you know - not only 'it was a trick'.
Never give false feedback about a learner's ability or personality in any lab.
limitations: University students; classic study; effect sizes and replications not reviewed here.

title: Debriefed but Still Troubled? About the (In)effectiveness of Postexperimental Debriefings after Ego Threat
publisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (APA)
key_findings: Six studies with false negative feedback about intelligence or attractiveness: written or in-person debriefings did not eliminate lowered well-being or hostile attributions; a prolonged, extensive personal debriefing worked best; affective effects lasted two weeks or more.
Internal meta-analyses: all debriefing versions helped somewhat but none fully restored baseline.
athar_applications: Strongest reason why ATHAR bias labs must NOT include any ego-threatening manipulation (no fake scores about the learner's intelligence, popularity or appearance) - debriefing cannot be relied on to undo it.
limitations: Adult samples; ego-threat manipulations differ from neutral contextual-information manipulations used in forensic-bias labs.

title: When a Negative Experience Sticks With You: Does the Revised Outcome Debriefing Counteract the Consequences of Experimental Ostracism in Psychological Research?
publisher: Journal of Empirical Research on Human Research Ethics (SAGE)
key_findings: Two studies using Cyberball exclusion: a potent revised outcome debriefing did not counteract decreased positive and increased negative mood; after-effects persisted more than one day.
athar_applications: Rules out any social-exclusion mechanic (e.g., in-game peers 'ignoring' the learner) as a bias-elicitation device for minors.
limitations: Adult samples; ostracism differs from contextual bias tasks.

title: Amelioration of Deception and Harm in Psychological Research: The Important Role of Debriefing
publisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (APA)
key_findings: Classic study on participants' reactions to deception and the role of debriefing in reducing perceived harm (record verified via Crossref; abstract not retrieved, finding characterised from its title and standard citation only).
athar_applications: Supporting citation that debriefing quality matters; ATHAR's operative rules rely on ATH-SRC-1745 and ATH-SRC-1746.
limitations: Not read beyond metadata; adult undergraduates.

title: Deception in Experiments: Revisiting the Arguments in Its Defense
publisher: Ethics & Behavior (Taylor & Francis)
key_findings: Reviews empirical evidence on whether deception undermines the experimental control it seeks: critics argue it makes participants suspicious and distorts behaviour; the paper weighs the evidence for these methodological costs (Ethics & Behavior 18(1): 59-92).
athar_applications: Product risk: repeated 'gotcha' labs could train learners to distrust every in-game clue and character, damaging fair-play mystery design - limit to one disclosed context lab per learning unit and never deceive about clue reliability in the main story.
limitations: Economics/psychology debate about research methodology, not education.

title: Deception in Medical and Behavioral Research: Is It Ever Acceptable?
publisher: The Milbank Quarterly
key_findings: Argues deception can be acceptable under specified conditions, centrally that subjects are informed before enrolling that the study may involve deception ('second order consent'); Milbank Quarterly 74(1): 87-114.
athar_applications: Basis for ATHAR's 'authorized surprise' rule: before any bias lab, learners (and for under-16s, parents via settings) are told that some labs deliberately hide or vary information and will explain it afterwards.
limitations: Medical/behavioural research context; only abstract-level content read.

title: Using the Barnum Effect to Teach about Ethics and Deception in Research
publisher: Teaching of Psychology (SAGE)
key_findings: University research-methods students received bogus personality feedback, rated its validity, were told of the deception and discussed its ethics; they accepted the feedback (seniors were more sceptical than juniors/sophomores) and agreed the approach helped them understand the costs and benefits of deception first-hand.
athar_applications: Precedent that experiential, disclosed classroom deception can teach - but it used personality feedback, which ATHAR forbids for minors (ego-relevant; see ATH-SRC-1746). ATHAR adapts only the structure: experience, reveal, discuss.
limitations: University students, not minors; single classroom report.

AUDIT-W2 2026-10-27: legal_text_access free_official -> paywalled: OpenAlex lists the article as closed (no OA copy); only the abstract is free. Metadata confirmed (Teaching of Psychology 20(1):33-35, Feb 1993); abstract supports the key finding.

title: Establishing a Safe Container for Learning in Simulation: The Role of the Presimulation Briefing
publisher: Simulation in Healthcare (Wolters Kluwer)
key_findings: Proposes practices that create a psychologically safe 'container': clarify expectations, establish a 'fiction contract' with participants, attend to logistics, and declare and enact respect and concern for learners' psychological safety.
athar_applications: Template for ATHAR's pre-lab briefing card (fiction contract: 'this lab may change what you see; mistakes here are data, not grades') and for teacher guides.
limitations: Healthcare simulation with adult professionals; practice synthesis rather than trial evidence.

title: The Role of Debriefing in Simulation-Based Learning
publisher: Simulation in Healthcare (Wolters Kluwer)
key_findings: Review article on the role of debriefing in simulation-based learning (Simulation in Healthcare 2(2): 115-125); PubMed lists no abstract, so only the title-level topic is used here.
athar_applications: Supports making the debrief a graded learning step in bias labs, not an optional pop-up.
limitations: Adult clinical simulation; not read in full.

title: The Teenage Brain: Sensitivity to Social Evaluation
publisher: Current Directions in Psychological Science (SAGE)
key_findings: Review: adolescents appear highly attuned to being evaluated by peers and respond to social-evaluative information with heightened emotional intensity, partly reflecting continuing brain development; evidence described as preliminary but mounting.
athar_applications: Why ATHAR bias labs must avoid public exposure of who was 'fooled': no leaderboards for bias labs, no sharing of individual errors with classmates, debriefs private and normalising ('most people, including experts, do this').
limitations: Narrative review; neuroscience-to-behaviour links are tentative; Western samples.

title: Learning from Errors
publisher: Annual Review of Psychology
key_findings: Review: errorful learning followed by corrective feedback benefits learning; high-confidence errors are corrected more readily than low-confidence ones (hypercorrection); corrective feedback including analysis of the reasoning behind the mistake is crucial; error tolerance encourages students.
athar_applications: Pedagogical justification for letting learners commit a contextual-bias error and then analyse it - provided feedback is immediate and explains the reasoning; supports recording confidence before reveal.
limitations: Mostly lab/classroom studies with neurotypical students; not specific to bias or deception.

title: Dark Patterns in the Design of Games
publisher: Foundations of Digital Games (FDG) 2013 proceedings
key_findings: Defines 'dark game design patterns' as patterns used by creators against players' interests, whose purpose can be argued to be questionable or unethical, and offers questions to identify them.
athar_applications: Check: a bias lab is ethical only if the 'trick' serves the player's learning interest, is disclosed, and has no monetisation or retention purpose - ATHAR adds a dark-pattern review to every lab with hidden information.
limitations: Conceptual taxonomy; examples not read in full.

title: Research Ethics Law on Living Creatures (Royal Decree No. M/59 of 14/9/1431H) - Saudi Arabia
title_ar: نظام أخلاقيات البحث على المخلوقات الحية
publisher: Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers (text as distributed by King Faisal University)
key_findings: Royal Decree M/59 dated 14/9/1431H (Council of Ministers decision 321 of 13/9/1431H); a printout of the official Bureau of Experts text distributed by King Faisal University.

Defines informed consent as 'الموافقة بعد التبصير' (consent given freely without coercion or exploitation after understanding what is requested, aims, risks, rights and duties), minor (القاصر) as under 18, guardian (الولي), and minimal risk (الخطر الأدنى).
Art. 25: research on a minor, a person lacking capacity or a disabled person is permitted only if the interest of these groups requires it; implementing regulations set the ethical controls.
athar_applications: Saudi legal vocabulary for the consent section of BIAS_LAB_ETHICS_FOR_MINORS.md (الموافقة بعد التبصير؛ الولي؛ الخطر الأدنى).

If ATHAR ever runs a STUDY (A/B test, efficacy evaluation) with Saudi minors, it falls under this law and needs an ethics committee; a commercial lesson is not automatically 'research', but data collection for evaluation may be.
limitations: Scope mainly biomedical; whether behavioural/educational evaluation of a game falls under it needs a Saudi lawyer; official BOE page blocked automated fetch (robots), so a university-hosted copy was read.

Related edition: the 07 pilot team catalogued the official English translation as ATH-SRC-2110 and its implementing regulations as ATH-SRC-2111; this record is the Arabic text - keep both, link at merge.

title: DNA explainer for families of missing persons (Arabic edition)
title_ar: شرح الحمض النووي لأسر المفقودين (اللجنة الدولية لشؤون المفقودين)
publisher: International Commission on Missing Persons
key_findings: One-page Arabic explainer (PDF created May 2024) describing DNA (الحمض النووي) as inherited genetic information, collection of reference samples (عيّنات) from relatives, DNA profiles (ملف حمض نووي) and a 'DNA match' (مطابقة الحمض النووي) result.
States that family participation is entirely voluntary, that families are informed in advance how their data will be used, and that consent is obtained before starting (موافقة).
athar_applications: Source for the plain-Arabic preferred term 'ملف الحمض النووي' (DNA profile) used in the glossary instead of the over-confident 'البصمة الوراثية', and for the consent-first framing of reference samples.
limitations: Outreach leaflet for missing-persons families - sensitive context; ATHAR uses terminology only, never this scenario.

title: An Overview of Criminal Proof and Its Modern Techniques
title_ar: نظرة عامة في الإثبات الجنائي وتقنياته الحديثة
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Arabic review (AJFSFM 3(1): 170-185) of modern scientific means in extracting forensic evidence and in criminal proof (الإثبات الجنائي).

Concludes that the use of scientific means is constrained by two issues: how far they intrude on the accused's fundamental rights and freedoms, and how conclusive their results are; rights should not be sacrificed (abstract).
athar_applications: Arab-published support for ATHAR's dual lesson: scientific evidence is powerful but limited, and its use is bounded by rights (links forensic labs to ARAB_CRIMINAL_PROCEDURE_CONTEXT.md).
Source for the term 'الإثبات الجنائي' (criminal proof).
limitations: Legal-review article; only the abstract was read.

title: Arabic translation: International Ethical Guidelines for Health-related Research Involving Humans (CIOMS 2016)
title_ar: الإرشادات الأخلاقية الدولية للبحوث المتعلقة بالصحة التي تشمل البشر (ترجمة عربية)
authors: Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences (CIOMS)
publisher: CIOMS
key_findings: CIOMS lists an Arabic translation (2020, 140 pages) of its 2016 international ethical guidelines, downloadable free after registration; the 2016 guidelines include a guideline on research involving children and adolescents.
athar_applications: Recommended Arabic-language ethics reference for an Arab ethics committee or child-protection reviewer assessing ATHAR's bias labs or any efficacy study with minors.
limitations: Not downloaded (registration form); translator not named; content not read - cited as a pointer only.
Related edition: the English CIOMS 2016 guidelines are catalogued by the 07 pilot team as ATH-SRC-2101; this record is the separate Arabic translation (2020).

title: Total Civilian Deaths During 2003-2015 and Post-Conflict Period in Iraq: Challenges and Achievements of the Medico-Legal Directorate (MLD) in Baghdad
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Bibliographic record (AJFSFM 1(5)) of an article by staff on the challenges and achievements of Iraq's Medico-Legal Directorate in Baghdad; content not read.
athar_applications: Used only to name the Iraqi national forensic-medicine authority (Medico-Legal Directorate, Baghdad) in the institutions map; its ministry affiliation (likely Ministry of Health) is not stated explicitly in the sources read.
limitations: Topic is conflict mortality - not usable for teen content; metadata only.

title: Stronger forensic services: Iraq and UAE exchange forensic experience and knowledge (UNODC study tour to Dubai, Nov 2021)
publisher: United Nations Iraq
key_findings: 8 Nov 2021: a UNODC project (2020-2023, US INL-funded) took a nine-member Iraqi delegation from the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Health (incl. the Medico-Legal Directorate) on a four-day study tour of Dubai Police's General Department of Forensic Science and Criminology (GD-FRC).
Planned outcomes: a forensic networking channel on drug trafficking and cooperation on forensic intelligence; the item does not mention accreditation.
athar_applications: Shows Dubai's GD-FRC acting as a regional reference/training hub and UNODC as the connector - relevant to partner strategy (a UNODC-linked Arab lab is a credible reviewer).
limitations: UN news item; no technical content.

title: Crime Scene and Physical Evidence Awareness for Non-forensic Personnel (ST/NAR/39) - Arabic edition (catalogue record)
title_ar: مسرح الجريمة والأدلة المادية: توعية الموظفين غير المتخصصين في التحليل الجنائي
publisher: United Nations (New York) / UNODC
key_findings: UN Library (Vienna) catalogue confirms ST/NAR/39 (Sales No. 09.IV.5; English ISBN 9789211302738; v, 25 p.) with an annex on types of physical evidence and their evidential value, and lists an Arabic edition titled 'مسرح الجريمة والأدلّة المادّية: توعية الموظفين غير المتخصّصين في التحليل الجنائي' (UNTERM renders the title 'توعية غير المتخصصين بكيفية التعامل مع مسرح الجريمة والأدلة المادية').
The English PDF is on the UN Digital Library (record 659283); no Arabic file link was found.
athar_applications: Highest-value Arabic terminology source still to obtain: an official UN Arabic text written for non-specialists (first responders) - the closest institutional analogue to ATHAR's teen register; to be requested from UNODC's Laboratory and Scientific Section.
limitations: Arabic content not read; existence verified by catalogue only.

title: Demographic Variability in Fingerprint Patterns
publisher: Naif Arab University for Security Sciences (Arab Journal of Forensic Sciences and Forensic Medicine)
key_findings: Study (AJFSFM 7(1): 18-33) of associations between age, blood group, caste and fingerprint pattern types in female participants in Bahawalpur, Pakistan; English text with an Arabic abstract and keywords.
The Arabic abstract uses 'أنماط بصمات الأصابع' and 'نمط العروة' (loop pattern); the Arabic labels for whorl/arch appear mismatched in the extracted text ('النمط المقوس'/'النمط الدائري').
athar_applications: Terminology only: attests 'نمط' alongside the UMD 'طراز' for fingerprint patterns, and shows inconsistency in Arabic pattern names even within the regional journal - supports listing pattern names as needing the terminology workshop.
limitations: Population-association study of limited relevance; ATHAR makes no use of its demographic claims (pattern-demographic links are not used for identification).
